latin.431: §. VI. Hoc pacto quidem Ortum suum nacta est Transsubstantiatio, sed obscurum privatumque, publicâ autoritate olim in lucem publicam emittenda, id quod Seculo demum XI. contigit.
latin.432: Cùm Berengarius Bertrami Orthodoxam quidem de Eucharistia Opinionem, multis etiam cum complicibus & asseclis secutus, crudè tamen nonnihil, panem consecratum, corporis Christi Figuram propemodum nudam, dicere visus est.
latin.433: Ob id, privatorum pariter atque publicorum Doctorum cumprimis Lanfranci Cantuariensis, seu istorum Antesignani, calamis confossus, à Papis Leone IX. anno 1049. & Nicolao II. anno 1059. non solum in judicium vocatus, sed & carceri mancipatus & ad recantationem his conceptam verbis adactus.
latin.434: Quibus omninò tùm Paschasii Rhadeberti de Convers. panis in corpus Christi, publicè confirmatur, quàm absurdissima ipsi Paschasio visa Laceratio corporis Christi dentalis solenniter introducitur.
latin.435: Ego Berengarius consentio S. Romanæ & Apostolicæ sedi & ore ac corde profiteor, de Sacramento Dominicæ mensæ eam fidem me tenere, quam Dominus & venerabilis Papa Nicolaus & hæc sacra Synodus Autoritate Evangelica & Apostolica tenendam tradidit mihique firmavit: panem scil. & vinum quæ in altari ponuntur post consecrationem non solummodo sacramentum, symbolum, sive figuram, sed etiam verum corpus & sanguinem Domini nostri Jesu Christi esse & SENSUALITER non solum sacramento, sed veritate manibus sacerdotum tractari, frangi & FIDELIUM DENTIBUS ATTERI, apud Gratianum de Consecr. dist. 2. c. 42.
latin.436: Quin tandem, cum Berengarius, ob negatam veritatem, sibi malè conscius, ad seipsum rediisset, & suam ipsius revocationem non minus absurdam quam impiam, scripto editô revocasset, eamque per vim sibi extortam esse ab Ecclesia malignantium & vanitatis Concilio, significasset, ab Hildebrando, aliis Hellenbrando, Gregorio VII. appellato, ad Romanum Concilium evocatus virgisque cæsus ad novam recantationem, trium mensium concessis induciis, coactus postliminio est, obtrusâ palinodiæ seu professionis ejusmodi formulâ, quâ panem mysticum substantialiter converti in veram & propriam carnem Christi, sub gravissimo Papæ præcepto, deinceps confitendum erat.
latin.437: Formulam Recantationis affert Thom. Waldensis, Tom. 2. cap. 24. & Abbas Uspergensis in Chronico ad annum 1080; Integram verò de Berengario historiam, ex doctissimi Usserii libro de successione Ecclesiarum cap. 7. à parag. 28. ad fin. capitis, in summam redactam evolve, in elaboratissima Historia Transsubstantiationis jam suprà commendati Johannis Dunelmensis cap. 7. §. 4. & seqq. à p. m. 134. ad pag. 143.

pass_a.431: §. VI. In this way indeed Transsubstantiation obtained its Ortus, but obscure and private, hereafter to be sent forth into public light by public authority — which at last happened in the eleventh Century.
pass_a.432: When Berengar, following indeed Bertram’s Orthodox Opinion concerning the Eucharist, even with many accomplices and followers, yet somewhat crudely seemed to say the consecrated bread was almost a naked Figure of Christ’s body.
pass_a.433: On that account, pierced by the pens of private as well as public Doctors, especially Lanfranc of Canterbury, or their standard-bearer, he was by Popes Leo IX in the year 1049 and Nicholas II in the year 1059 not only called into judgment, but also committed to prison and driven to a recantation conceived in these words.
pass_a.434: By which altogether then Paschasius Radbertus’s [teaching] on the Conversion of bread into Christ’s body is publicly confirmed, and that dental Laceration of Christ’s body — which seemed most absurd even to Paschasius himself — is solemnly introduced.
pass_a.435: I Berengar agree with the Holy Roman and Apostolic See and profess with mouth and heart that concerning the Sacrament of the Lord’s table I hold that faith which the Lord and venerable Pope Nicholas and this sacred Synod by Evangelical and Apostolic Authority handed to be held and confirmed to me: namely that the bread and wine which are placed on the altar after consecration are not only a sacrament, symbol, or figure, but also the true body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and are SENSUALLY handled, broken, and WORN BY THE FAITHFUL’S TEETH not only in sacrament but in truth by the priests’ hands — in Gratian, De Consecr. dist. 2 c. 42.
pass_a.436: Nay at length, when Berengar, ill at ease with himself for having denied the truth, had returned to himself and by a published writing revoked his own revocation as no less absurd than impious, and had signified that it had been extorted from him by force by a Council of the malignant Church and of vanity, he was summoned by Hildebrand (by others Hellenbrand), called Gregory VII, to a Roman Council and beaten with rods to a new recantation; three months’ truce being granted, he was afterward compelled, a palinode or profession of this sort being thrust upon him, by which under the Pope’s most grave precept it was thereafter to be confessed that the mystic bread is substantially converted into the true and proper flesh of Christ.
pass_a.437: Thomas Netter of Walden alleges the Formula of Recantation, Tom. 2 ch. 24, and the Abbot of Ursperg in the Chronicle at the year 1080; but unroll the whole history of Berengar, reduced to a summary from the most learned Ussher’s book on the succession of the Churches ch. 7 from §28 to the end of the chapter, in the most elaborate History of Transsubstantiation already praised above of John of Durham ch. 7 §. 4 and following from p. 134 to p. 143.

431: §.VI: Transsubstantiation has its Ortus — but still obscure and private.
Public authority will push it into public light only in the eleventh century.
432: Berengar follows Bertram’s orthodox Eucharist opinion (with many allies).
Yet he seems to speak crudely: consecrated bread almost a naked Figure of Christ’s body.
433: Private and public doctors — Lanfranc of Canterbury foremost — pierce him with their pens.
Leo IX (1049) and Nicholas II (1059) haul him to judgment, prison, and a forced recantation.
434: That recantation publicly confirms Paschasius’s conversion of bread into Christ’s body.
It also solemnly introduces the dental laceration of Christ’s body — which Paschasius himself had found most absurd.
435: Ego Berengarius: after consecration the altar bread and wine are not only sacrament/symbol/figure but the true body and blood.
And SENSUALLY — in truth, not only in sacrament — priests’ hands handle and break them, and the faithful’s teeth wear them (Gratian De Consecr. dist. 2 c. 42).
436: Berengar, conscience-struck, published a revocation of that forced palinode as absurd and impious, calling the council a church of the malignant and of vanity.
Hildebrand (Gregory VII) summoned him to Rome, beat him with rods, and after a three-month truce forced a new formula: mystic bread substantially converted into Christ’s true proper flesh.
437: Recantation formula: Thomas Walden Tom. 2 ch. 24; Abbot of Ursperg Chronicle at 1080.
Full Berengar history: Ussher De successione Ecclesiarum ch. 7 §§28–end, summarized in John of Durham’s Historia Transsubstantiationis ch. 7 §.4 ff. pp. 134–143.
Stop before §.VII (public monster seated by papal decrees / Lateran name).
